title: Adaptive curator circuit with Bayesian spike detector and stratified fallback
creator: Lena Patel
description:
Problem: sudden, correlated latency and error spikes against upstream model dependencies and tenant bursts are causing multi-region failovers and noisy SLO violations. Existing threshold-based breakers are brittle to short lived spikes and either trip too late (causing cascading failures) or too early (unnecessary fallbacks, hurting quality).

Proposal: implement an 'Adaptive Curator Circuit' -- a per-entity (tenant/model/dependency) circuit controller that: 1) runs a lightweight Bayesian online spike/change detector on latency and error-rate streams to infer probability of an ongoing degradation; 2) translates the detector's posterior into a graded 'curation score' with confidence; 3) maps curation scores to stratified fallback actions (soft-throttle, model-variant reroute, synthetic degraded response, or denial) with deterministic backoff windows; 4) integrates with multi-region routing so that cross-region migration follows policy and avoids amplifying load; 5) persists minimal state (exponential decay counters + confidence) in a distributed TTL store to enable cross-instance coordination during canaries and failovers.

Goals: reduce SLO breaches during short-lived spikes, provide predictable and auditable fallbacks, and enable safe automated reroutes across regions while preserving quality where possible.
design_decisions: Use Bayesian online changepoint detector (BOCD variant) for low-latency, incremental computation of spike probability rather than pure percentiles or moving-window thresholds.
Store compact state per-entity in Redis with 30s-5min TTLs; avoid heavy per-request DB hits. State includes running sufficient statistics and last-decision timestamp.
Expose deterministic mapping from curation score -> action to make fallbacks auditable and testable (no random flipping).

Implement stratified fallback tiers: T1 soft-throttle (sample-based shedding), T2 route to cheaper / quantized model variant, T3 synthetic degraded response with structured explanation, T4 deny (last resort).
Integrate with routing plane so that region migration honors tenancy affinity and avoids global amplification (circuit status travels with request metadata).
Make the system opt-in per-customer with global defaults; enterprise tenants can opt for strict isolation or manual overrides.
Prefer simulation-driven calibration before rollout: run fault-injection trials against historical traffic trace replay to tune thresholds and confidence cutoffs.
Security: decisions must be logged to audit pipeline; logs should not include PII or prompt contents.
Fail-safe: if state store becomes unavailable, fall back to conservative soft-throttle (sample-based shedding) rather than full open circuit.
Expose observability: per-entity SLO impact, curation score histogram, decisions timeline, and canary comparisons in console.
Avoid per-token intervention; make fallbacks at request level to maintain throughput and simplify client semantics.
acceptance_criteria: Simulation: run replay of 72 hours of production traces with injected spikes; measured SLO (p95 latency and error rate) regressions reduced by >=40% compared to current threshold breaker in equivalent failure scenarios.
Canary: deploy to 5% of traffic for non-enterprise tenants in regional pair (us-west/us-east) for 72 hours with automated rollback on >5% additional SLO breaches.
Observability: new dashboards show per-entity curation score, action histograms, and a searchable decision-log for the last 30 days.
Safety: when the state store is unavailable, system falls back to documented conservative soft-throttle behavior and logs incident; this behavior is validated in chaos run.
Docs & Runbook: design doc, ops playbook, and customer-facing behavior page published and reviewed by SRE and Product (links added).
Tests: unit tests for BOCD computations, integration tests for persisted state and decision mapping, and end-to-end integration in staging with synthetic spike generator.

notes: Trade-offs: BOCD gives probabilistic detection and is more robust to short bursts but requires careful calibration of priors; choosing too aggressive priors may over-react and cause quality loss.
Alternative considered: percentile-based adaptive window with hysteresis; rejected because it performed poorly on small-sample tenants and had higher false positive rate in simulations.
State persistence size: expect ~200k keys at peak with 100k active entities; each key ~400 bytes, memory budgeting required (see infra estimate).

Fallback content policy: synthetic degraded responses must include structured 'degraded:true' field and a human-friendly short explanation; customers can configure different degrade-response templates.
Observability signal design: prefer high-cardinality logs for decision debug but aggregate for standard dashboards to avoid cost blowup.

Operational hazard: risk of cascading global failover if routing plane duplicates traffic during failback; mitigation: introduce tokenized handshakes and backpressure signals when migrating between regions.
